messages:
elena_finance: FYI Velox reached out — they're seeing a billing spike and claim it was triggered by a rate-cap proration that moved them into the next tier for Mar 31. They want an audit + candidate credit.

tom_cs: Got the thread from Velox. They attached invoice lines and say the effective per-1k rate jumped after our proration. They want to know if the proration logic double-counted a small outage window.

maya_fin: Can you paste the invoice lines or the invoice id? I need to see the exact SKU and tier boundaries.

tom_cs: Invoice INV-2026-VE-0897, lines 12-15. Quick snippet: "Streaming tokens: 1,021,450 @ $0.0062/1k" then "Proration adj: +$3,120" — they argue the adj shouldn't have elevated the per-unit price.

ryan_sre: On March 31 we had an autoscaling anomaly in us-west causing a 22m pause (00:48-01:10 UTC) where requests were retried to other regions. Our ratecap controller applied proration at hour boundary; there might be an aggregation bug when cross-region retries are present.

sam_ops: Running an audit against token metering and ratecap windows. SQL: 
```
SELECT account_id, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(prorated_hours) as pror_hours
FROM ratecap_ledger
WHERE account_id = 'velox' AND day = '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY account_id;
```
Will run and share counts.

lina_eng: Flag: we changed the proration logic last quarter to prefer region-affinity for hourly buckets; it's possible retries with forwarded headers caused tokens to be counted in both origin and target buckets. Small chance of double-counting.

replay-bot: started replay job replay-2071-ratecap-velox for window 2026-03-31T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-31T03:00:00Z (eta ~9m).

sam_ops: First-pass results: Velox tokens on Mar 31 = 1,027,832; prorated_hours aggregated = 1.05 (expected ~1). Suspect ~2.5% inflation due to cross-region retry attribution.

maya_fin: If it's 2.5% inflation, what's the dollar impact? Need estimate to propose credit.

ryan_sre: Baseline: 1,021,450 tokens billed at their tier price $0.0062/1k = $6.33 ~ wait that's off, recalc: 1,021,450/1000 * 0.0062 = $6.33? That doesn't match invoice. Is the per-1k rate actually $6.20?

lina_eng: Clarify: their negotiated rate is $6.20 per 1k tokens (enterprise tier) not $0.0062. Unit confusion often happens in exports. So invoice numbers make more sense.

maya_fin: ok. Using $6.20 per 1k: a 2.5% overcount on 1,021,450 tokens = ~25,536 extra tokens => billed delta ~= (25.536 * $6.20) = $158.33k? That seems large; double-check math.

sam_ops: Recalc carefully: tokens in thousands = 1,021.45 k. 2.5% of that = 25.536 k. 25.536 * $6.20 = $158,323.2. Yes the enterprise rates are per 1k tokens and are high here.

elena_finance: That's material. Velox is a large account; we need to be precise. Before any credit: 1) full replay artifacts, 2) proof of double attribution, 3) check that credit won't change their committed tier thresholds unintentionally.

replay-bot: replay job replay-2071-ratecap-velox completed. Artifacts: s3://replay-exports/replay-2071-ratecap-velox.json. Reconstructed duplicate-attribution events = 25,478 tokens (25.478k).

lina_eng: The replay shows tokens duplicated across us-west and eu-proxy due to forwarded-retry header missing a dedup id. Patch ENG-9539 will add a idempotency header for cross-region forward retries and will alter ledger aggregation to dedupe by retry_id. Small DB migration planned.

sam_ops: After dedupe, reconstructed true missing delta = 25,478 tokens. Dollar impact (25.478k * $6.20) = $157,003.6.

maya_fin: Given the size, finance director sign-off required. Also we need to consider whether applying a credit retroactively causes them to drop below committed volume discounts; that could harm us. Run a committed-tier impact model.

elena_finance: I will run impact model. If credit would reduce their committed tier status, propose two options: 1) issue full credit and offer a small rebate to keep them at same tier, or 2) issue pro-rated credit but keep tier intact. Need legal/CS input.

tom_cs: Velox prefers fast resolution. They asked for a credit and a short postmortem. Also asked if we can prevent future proration surprises.

maya_fin: For now, hold issuing credit until impact model done. If legal/OPS ok, I can approve up to $200k provisional while we finalize wording.

elena_finance: I ran the model: with credit applied, Velox would slip below the quarterly committed threshold resulting in an extra $45k in true-up risk for us. Recommendation: issue full credit of $157,004 and simultaneously apply a one-time retention adjustment of $45,000 to keep their effective tier unchanged. Total commercial concession = $202,004.

lina_eng: We'll fast-track ENG-9539 and post the patch note. ETA for migration + deploy: 48h.

replay-bot: recorded audit trail: s3://replay-exports/replay-2071-ratecap-velox.json, bill-audit://BILL-AUDIT-2071.

elena_finance: Approve total concession $202,004. Please create BILL-1134 with attachments and a customer message draft.

tom_cs: Draft to Velox: "We're sorry — we found a proration aggregation bug that inflated your March 31 usage by ~2.5%. We've applied a $157,004 credit and a one-time retention adjustment of $45,000 to preserve your committed tier. We've deployed a fix and added dedupe monitoring. Happy to schedule a walkthrough."

maya_fin: LGTM. :+1:

sam_ops: Created BILL-1134, attached replay artifacts, ENG-9539 link, and queued credit for next invoice run.

elena_finance: Thanks team. Please post a short incident summary to incidents channel and keep all artifacts for audit.
